Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PCP^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2 \times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PCP^{-1},$ where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/489a26b52ac132d82ffa918d931963a0cd33df092aea8e70885dc41c4e363be5.svg)

and $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda.$

- From the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/bfc2be5324b72df4c3c63e92c4501bbda6b0fcde0ef8e6284d739db51e73a722.svg) we deduce that $\textrm{Re}(\lambda)={\color{blue}3}$ and $\textrm{Im}(\lambda) = {\color{red}-1}.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda = {\color{blue}3}+({\color{red}-1})\text{i} = 3-\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/1fd5d191e88cd5f00ffd91f83800ce0c82024cedea60bf78432cd0abb504252a.svg) we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14244484/assets/df9978ae9ef1bb16b79e36abace84ef559ef64b6aa9e47369ae7efc5ecf7da27.svg)

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{v}.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are
